user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a next-generation proteasome inhibitor in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, targeting patients with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a prior PI. The trial will be conducted globally across the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will need NICE and ICER submissions. The mechanism involves weekly IV administration with step-up dosing in Cycle 1. Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** The trial aims to demonstrate the proteasome inhibitor's superiority through patient-reported improvements in bone pain, physical functioning, and fatigue preservation versus standard of care.

**Key challenge:**  No validated bone pain instrument exists for multiple myeloma despite pain being a significant predictor of EQ-5D utility values and pre-selected as clinically relevant in previous assessments .

**Recommended starting point:**  EORTC QLQ-C30 with MY20 module — demonstrated significant change detection in TOURMALINE-MM3, A.R.R.O.W., and ENDEAVOR trials ;  BFI for fatigue measurement with established 1.33-point MCID ;  EQ-5D-5L mandatory for HTA submissions .

**Critical gap:** Disease-related bone pain domain lacks a validated instrument candidate despite being an FDA core concept and primary TPP claim.

## Table 1: Domain Coverage Comparison

| FDA Core Concept | Source | Current Trial Candidates | IKEMA 2021 | TOURMALINE-MM4 2020 | TOURMALINE-MM3 2019 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disease-related bone pain | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | No instrument found | EORTC QLQ-C30 ❌ Pain subscale only | EORTC QLQ-C30 ❌ Pain subscale only | EORTC QLQ-C30 ✅ Change: Y [TI-003] |
| Physical function | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | ECOG PS (score 60, change: Yes) | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected |
| Fatigue | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | BFI (score 68, change: Yes) | EORTC QLQ-C30 ⚠️ General (fatigue subscale only) | EORTC QLQ-C30 ⚠️ General (fatigue subscale only) | EORTC QLQ-C30 ✅ Change: Y [TI-003] |
| Symptomatic adverse events | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | No instrument found | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected |
| Side effect impact summary | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | No instrument found | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected |
| Role function | FDA 2024 Core PRO Guidance | No instrument found | EORTC QLQ-C30 ✅ Change: NR [TI-001] | EORTC QLQ-C30 ✅ Change: NR [TI-002] | EORTC QLQ-C30 ✅ Change: Y [TI-003] |
| HTA Utility | NICE/ICER Requirements | EQ-5D-5L | EQ-5D-5L ✅ Change: NR [TI-001] | ❌ Not collected | ❌ Not collected |

## Table 2: PRO Measures Comparison

| Trial | Year | Drug | Drug class | PRO Measures (n items) | Calibrated SOA | Total items | Est. time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IKEMA [TI-001] | 2021 | carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20), EQ-5D-5L (5) | No | 55 | 19-25 min |
| TOURMALINE-MM4 [TI-002] | 2020 | ixazomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) | No | 50 | 17-22 min |
| TOURMALINE-MM3 [TI-003] | 2019 | ixazomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) | No | 50 | 17-22 min |
| A.R.R.O.W. [TI-004] | 2018 | carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | CSQ-8 (8), EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20), EQ-5D-5L (5) | No | 63 | 21-28 min |
| ENDEAVOR [TI-005] | 2016 | carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), FACT/GOG-NTX (n=?), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) | No | 50+ | 17+ min |
| Current Trial (Proposed) | 2026 | Next-gen PI | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30), EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20), BFI (9), EQ-5D-5L (5) | TBD — expert decision required | 64 | 21-28 min |

## Key Observations

•  In proteasome inhibitor trials, EORTC QLQ-C30 achieved significant change detection in TOURMALINE-MM3 (p<0.05), A.R.R.O.W. (partial), and ENDEAVOR (p<0.001) , providing robust evidence of sensitivity in this mechanism class.

•  Ixazomib trials show mixed PRO outcomes — TOURMALINE-MM4 had null results (EMA rejection) while TOURMALINE-MM3 was significant, suggesting trial design factors beyond instrument selection affect detectability .

•  FDA's 2026 draft guidance prioritizes MRD endpoints for accelerated approval, potentially reducing regulatory emphasis on PRO-based labelling claims , though survival-based confirmatory trials will still require PRO evidence.

•  EORTC QLQ-MY20 provides myeloma-specific context but adds little to EQ-5D utility prediction compared to QLQ-C30 alone (R² 0.70 vs 0.69)  — consider item reduction strategy.

•  QLQ-C30 and MY20 have established MCID thresholds (10 points for most scales) but rarely result in FDA/EMA label claims as standalone evidence  — typically supportive only.

•  Recent Chinese validation shows moderate correlations between EQ-5D-5L and QLQ-C30 (r=0.545 in MM patients), with QLU-C10D showing stronger correlation (r=0.772)  — consider QLU-C10D as alternative utility measure.

## Comparator Analysis

 Carfilzomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (GHS/QoL only) | EMA accepted | Trial must differentiate from carfilzomib's established peripheral neuropathy burden through superior PRO tolerability profile .

 Ixazomib | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-MY20 | EMA accepted | Oral dosing convenience of ixazomib sets high bar for demonstrating meaningful patient burden differences with IV administration .

 Bortezomib, selinexor, and panobinostat comparators show limited or negative PRO precedents , creating opportunity for positive differentiation if trial design adequately powers PRO endpoints.

Based on comparator evidence,  EORTC QLQ-C30 has the strongest signal of change detection in proteasome inhibitor mechanisms, with A.R.R.O.W. achieving p<0.001 for carfilzomib and ENDEAVOR showing significant results .

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In candidate list? | Action needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include — mandatory for QALY calculation |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include — mandatory for cost-effectiveness analysis |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1.  Whether to accept QLQ-C30 pain subscale as proxy for disease-related bone pain domain given lack of myeloma-specific bone pain instruments .

2.  Whether to reduce patient burden by using QLQ-C30 subscales rather than full instrument — no comparator trials used calibrated SOA approach .

3.  PRO endpoint positioning within testing hierarchy — 90% of KG trials used PRO as secondary endpoints, suggesting standard practice for confirmatory positioning behind survival endpoints .

4. Weekly IV assessment schedule alignment with step-up dosing in Cycle 1 and patient burden considerations over extended treatment duration.

5.  Whether to add BFI and ECOG PS despite limited regulatory precedent as primary evidence in MM submissions .
